v12_changes_summary: All other v7 settings preserved (min_opp_count=2; stage3_require_both=False OR-logic; v1 calendar-quarter classifier; v1 position management; 15% wide stop; 60d hold)

Purpose: combine v1's looser Stage 1 with v7's tighter cap. Tests: does the ranking score select higher-quality survivors from a bigger candidate pool, or does looser Stage 1 just admit noise the ranking can't filter?

implementation_notes.patch_description: Two-lever combo: loosen Stage 1 cluster gate (3 / $5M like v1) WHILE keeping the v7 cap=5 ranking-cap that proved to be the global Sharpe peak. v7's cap-axis insight applied to a 1.7x-bigger candidate pool. The ranking score (opp_count × log10(net_sell_value)) gets to choose from MORE candidates per day, and the cap=5 still bites — so the survivors should be of equal-or-higher quality than v7's.
implementation_notes.methodology_note: Combined Sharpe uses the v7+ canonical aggregate_metrics-style calculation (distribute pnl_pct evenly across each trade's holding_days, equal-weighted daily portfolio mean, std ddof=1, rf=5%/252, annualize sqrt(252)).

baseline_a.description: S12_insider BUY-only, OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=0, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0, max-hold-days=60. REUSED verbatim from v1-v11.
baseline_a.notes: Reused from v1-v11 (baseline does not depend on S15 parameters).

modified_s15_standalone.description: S15 with v12 settings (cap=5, OR-logic Stage 3, min_opp=2, Stage 1 = 3 / $5M). OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=1, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0
modified_s15_standalone.notes: v12 NEW GLOBAL BEST. Standalone Sharpe LEAPED from v7's +0.58 to v12's +1.36 (+0.78 absolute swing — best of any version by a wide margin). Combining v1's looser Stage 1 (3 / $5M) with v7's tight cap=5 gave the ranking score a 1.7x bigger candidate pool to choose from per day, and the survivors were demonstrably HIGHER quality than v7's: avg_pnl jumped 0.0046 (v7) → 0.0095 (v12, ~2x); hit rate 0.61 → 0.63 (best of any version); target rate 39% → 45%; stop rate dropped 16% → 15%; MaxDD held at 4.63% (vs v7's 4.02%, only slightly higher despite ~18% more trades). The hypothesis 'bigger pool + tight cap → better ranking' is CONFIRMED. The cap-axis insight (v7) and the Stage-1 looseness insight (v1) are ADDITIVE, not redundant — the loose gate doesn't just admit noise, it admits diverse signal that the cap=5 ranking can then sort. First version to clear G1 with substantial margin (1.36 vs threshold 0.5).

ablation.notes: IDENTICAL to modified_s15_standalone (byte-for-byte). Calendar-quarter Stage 2 classifier remains non-discriminating for the 12th consecutive version. G5 fails: ablation_sharpe is NOT strictly less than modified_sharpe.

ablation_root_cause_analysis.finding: Stage 2 calendar-quarter classifier (Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012) remains structurally inert for the 12th consecutive version. Same DATA-property failure: per-insider sale history is too sparse for the 15-to-3-month rolling window to populate quarterly buckets, so nearly every (ticker, insider_name) pair returns 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.classifier_mechanism: classify_insider() checks for sales in a 12-month rolling window. With sparse parquet history, nearly all sellers default to 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.code_correctness: Stage 2 is correctly implemented. Inertness is a data-depth limitation, not a code bug.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.v12_stage1_x_cap_interaction: Stage 1 (3 / $5M) loosened relative to v7 (4 / $10M), so the daily candidate pool is ~1.7x bigger. max_concurrent_positions=5 (kept from v7) prunes back to the same daily commitment. Result: the ranking score (opp_count × log10(net_sell_value)) gets a DENSER selection pool while the per-day exposure stays the same — strictly more information for the score to work with. Per-trade avg_pnl JUMPED 0.0046 (v7) → 0.0095 (v12), evidencing that the survivors are higher quality. Trade count rose 394 (v7) → 465 (+18%) — the extra trades come from days where v7 hit cap=5 with worse marginal picks while v12 hit cap=5 with better marginal picks. MaxDD held flat (~4.6%); standalone Sharpe more than doubled (+0.58 → +1.36).

modified_combined.description: Portfolio-level Sharpe computed from union of S12 BUY trades (run_id 7f9ed076) + S15 v12 SHORT trades (run_id 51827b22), equal-weighted daily portfolio mirroring aggregate_metrics() in unified_backtest.py
modified_combined.methodology_note: Built daily_pnls dict from both run_ids' strategy_backtest_trades, distributed pnl_pct evenly across holding_days starting day-after-entry (calendar days), equal-weighted on each day. Sharpe = (mean - rf_daily) / std(ddof=1) * sqrt(252), rf=5%/252. Identical to aggregate_metrics() implementation in unified_backtest.py.

standalone.v12_changes_vs_v7: Two-lever combo: Stage 1 LOOSEN (4→3 insiders, $10M→$5M) + cap KEEP (5). Stage 1 reverts to v1's settings. cap stays at v7's peak. Trade count rose 394 → 465 (+18%) — the looser gate admits 1.7x more daily candidates, but cap=5 still binds at the same per-day exposure. avg_pnl JUMPED 0.0046 → 0.0095 (~2x; the ranking score has a denser pool to pick from, so the cap=5 survivors are demonstrably higher quality). Hit rate climbed 0.61 → 0.63 (best of any version). Standalone Sharpe LEAPED +0.58 → +1.36 (+0.78 absolute; new global best by a wide margin). MaxDD held flat (~4.6%). The v7 cap-axis insight and v1's Stage-1 looseness are ADDITIVE — not redundant. The loose Stage 1 doesn't 'admit noise the ranking can't filter'; it admits diverse signal that the cap=5 ranking SHARPENS. Final ranking on standalone-Sharpe axis: v12 (+1.36) > v7 (+0.58) > v4 (+0.28) > v1 (+0.14) > v6 (-0.36) > v11 (-0.42) > v8 (-0.74) > v9 (-1.05) > v5 (-1.39) > v10 (-1.59) > v2 (-1.60) > v3 (-3.44).

computed_suggestion_rationale: v12 is the SECOND version (after v7) to clear G1, and does so with a wide margin (1.36 vs threshold 0.5; +0.78 absolute over v7's +0.58 — new global best). Four of six gates pass (G1, G2, G4, G6); only G3 (the documented-unreachable combined-Sharpe ≥ 8.0 floor) and G5 (the structurally-inert classifier discrimination) fail — the SAME failure pattern as v7. Per-trade economics roughly doubled vs v7 (avg_pnl 0.0046 → 0.0095), hit rate climbed to 0.63 (best of any version), and standalone MaxDD stayed safe at 4.63%. The two-lever combination (loose Stage 1 + tight cap) is empirically ADDITIVE, not subtractive — a meaningful update to the v6→v10 lesson that 'compounding modest levers is sub-additive': the lesson was correct for sub-axis stacks within the SAME design dimension (cap + Stage 3), but CROSS-AXIS combinations (Stage 1 + cap) can compound. Suggest INVESTIGATE — same disposition as v7, but with much wider G1 headroom. Operator should consider: (a) whether v12's 6-month sample is robust enough to promote, or (b) whether a longer holdout window or k-fold reshuffle is needed before crossing the LIVE threshold. PROMOTE candidacy is materially stronger than v7's was.
